requirement_text.REQ-054: Port src/engine/snapshot_writer.zig (348 lines -- R-Co's ISS-601, design artefact src/design/iss601_state_snapshots.md) as Letflow.Engine.SnapshotWriter, plus its instance_state_snapshots migration and Ecto.Schema module (schema-per-tenant per REQ-022, same as every other table this stage adds). THIS REQUIREMENT EXTENDS REQ-053's already-shipped reconstruct path -- it is not a standalone module. REQ-053 builds full-log replay from sequence 1; this requirement adds the snapshot table, the writer, and the replay-source selection that lets that same reconstruct function start from the latest snapshot instead. The deliverable is therefore a modification of REQ-053's function plus new supporting code, and the correctness bar below is that both paths agree. Purpose: reconstruction (REQ-053) replaying the FULL event log from sequence 1 is O(events) and gets slower forever. A periodic snapshot of the InstanceState as a jsonb blob lets reconstruction replay only the events SINCE the latest snapshot. - take_snapshot/N: serialises REQ-044's InstanceState (status, tokens, variables, pending task nodes, error_detail) plus the sequence_number it is current as of, into an instance_state_snapshots row. - maybe_take_snapshot/N: the cadence check -- snapshot every N events, default 1000 per snapshot_writer.zig's DEFAULT_SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL. Called after event appends and on instance completion. - REQ-053's replay-source selection: given a latest snapshot at sequence S, replay only events with sequence_number > S on top of the deserialised snapshot state, versus replaying from 1 when no snapshot exists (reconstruction.zig's determineReplaySourceForSnapshot()). This requirement extends REQ-053's reconstruct path to use snapshots when present -- and the correctness bar is that BOTH paths produce the identical state, since a snapshot that diverges from full replay is worse than no snapshot at all. - This table is NOT the same thing as REQ-027/REQ-033's instance_definition_snapshots (the immutable PD-08 DEFINITION graph bound to an instance at start). These are periodic EXECUTION STATE snapshots, mutable in the sense that new rows accumulate over an instance's life. Say so explicitly in the moduledoc -- the two names are one word apart and confusing them would be a silent data-model error. OPEN QUESTION (flag, do not silently resolve): where the events-since-last-snapshot counter lives. instance_projections.last_event_seq (REQ-023) already tracks the latest sequence per instance, which makes a pure row-based cadence check possible with no in-memory counter at all; R-Co's own SnapshotWriter is a struct holding a pool handle. If REQ-045 resolved to supervised processes, an in-process counter is available but is exactly the kind of state stage-3-instance-engine.md's second Early finding warns is NOT automatically worth a process. Leave the choice to CODE-DESIGNER, citing that finding and REQ-045's resolution.

task.description: Validate test/specs/REQ-054.md and test/letflow/engine/snapshot_writer_test.exs (commit 9d1ea98 on feature/WF02-REQ054-20260819). TEST-DESIGNER flagged one genuine gap in its own handoff: AC6 (maybe_take_snapshot cadence firing from real engine.ex call sites at the default interval of 1000) could not be proven end-to-end because REQ-028's @max_nodes 500 graph cap makes it structurally impossible for one instance to accumulate 1000 real events through create/2+complete_task/3 alone. TEST-DESIGNER covered this instead with (a) a real-call-site test proving no premature write below threshold, and (b) a separate test feeding a real Engine-produced InstanceState into maybe_take_snapshot/4 with a small interval override to prove the write half fires. Independently judge whether this is adequate coverage or a real gap requiring rework.
acceptance_criteria: priv/repo/migrations gains an instance_state_snapshots migration, schema-per-tenant per REQ-022, applying cleanly against a provisioned tenant schema
take_snapshot writes a row whose deserialised state equals the InstanceState passed in, round-tripped field-for-field including tokens and variables
maybe_take_snapshot writes no row before the interval is reached and exactly one row when it is, with the interval configurable and defaulting to 1000

reconstructing an instance that has a snapshot at sequence S replays only events with sequence_number greater than S, and produces a state identical to the same instance reconstructed with snapshots ignored entirely -- an explicit both-paths-agree test, not just a faster-path test
the moduledoc explicitly distinguishes instance_state_snapshots (periodic execution state, this requirement) from instance_definition_snapshots (immutable PD-08 definition graph, REQ-027/REQ-033)
the moduledoc names the snapshot-cadence-counter placement as an open question left for CODE-DESIGNER, citing stage-3-instance-engine.md's second Early finding and REQ-045's process-vs-row resolution

result.summary: Independently read test/specs/REQ-054.md and test/letflow/engine/snapshot_writer_test.exs (not TEST-DESIGNER's summary) and checked each of the 6 acceptance criteria against actual test code: AC1 (migration, no tenant_id column) -> 'AC1 -- instance_state_snapshots migration' describe block, real information_schema.columns query. AC2 (round-trip field-for-field incl. nil token fields) -> two tests in 'AC2 -- take_snapshot/4 round trip', using rich_instance_state_fixture (2 tokens, nested variables, join_counters with all 3 MapSet fields) and minimal_instance_state_fixture (nil branch_id/waiting_child_instance_id). AC3 (default 1000 + configurable cadence) -> two tests in 'AC3 -- maybe_take_snapshot/4 cadence', asserting :skipped/no-row below threshold and :snapshotted/exactly-one-row at threshold for both the literal default and an interval: 5 override. AC4 (both-paths-agree, INV-ISS-1) -> 'AC4 -- both-paths-agree' test, two real instances (A snapshotted mid-way via a real SnapshotWriter.take_snapshot/4 call, B never snapshotted forcing {:full_replay, 1}), asserts event_count 1 vs 4 (proving the snapshot path was genuinely taken, not coincidental convergence) plus assert_instance_states_agree on node-id multiset/variables/status/pending-task-nodes. AC5 (moduledoc distinguishes instance_state_snapshots from instance_definition_snapshots, and names the cadence-counter open question citing stage-3-instance-engine.md + req045) -> two tests in 'AC5 -- SnapshotWriter moduledoc content' asserting on Code.fetch_docs/1 output. AC6 (engine.ex wiring, real end-to-end) -> two tests: 'no premature write' drives real Engine.create/2, Engine.complete_task/3, and Engine.set_instance_error/2 through their real call sites and confirms latest_snapshot/2 stays :snapshot_not_found while last_event_sequence_number < 1000; 'writes once its real threshold holds' takes an InstanceState/sequence_number a real Engine.complete_task/3 call actually produced and passes it through the identical SnapshotWriter.maybe_take_snapshot/4 function engine.ex's call sites invoke, with a real interval: 1 override (a documented cadence_opts() field, not a stub), and confirms a row is written and round-trips correctly. Independently judged the AC6 gap TEST-DESIGNER flagged: read engine.ex's three wiring functions (maybe_snapshot_after_create/4 lines 559-586, maybe_snapshot_after_complete_task/2 lines 1005-1039, maybe_snapshot_after_set_instance_error/3 lines 2066-2089) and confirmed they are thin pass-throughs that call SnapshotWriter.maybe_take_snapshot/4 with the real instance_id/instance_state/sequence_number/prefix and no interval override (so the real default of 1000 applies) -- none contains branching logic whose correctness depends on the literal magnitude of the interval, so no bug class exists in the wiring itself that only a genuine 1000-real-event end-to-end run could catch. REQ-028's @max_nodes 500 graph cap (lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex:158) makes accumulating 1000 real events through create/2+complete_task/3 alone structurally impossible, and set_instance_error/2's own eligibility check rejects a second call once :error, closing off a 999-call-plus-one workaround. Given that, the two-test split (a: proves the real wiring correctly evaluates real arguments and never fires early; b: proves the identical shared function genuinely writes once threshold holds, using real Engine-produced data) combined with AC3's already-isolated proof that the literal default constant is 1000, jointly cover the full contract without a manufactured always-passing test. This is adequate, not a gap requiring rework. Also verified: no @tag :skip anywhere in the file (the two 'skipped' hits are :skipped return-value assertions, not skip tags), no 'TODO: implement test' in the spec, every test calls provisioned_tenant() independently (fresh tenant + schema + on_exit cleanup per test, Sandbox :auto mode) so tests are self-sufficient with no shared hardcoded IDs (unique_name/1 and unique_idempotency_key/1 use System.unique_integer/1), and no hardcoded secrets or connection strings anywhere in the test file or spec (grep confirmed). Ran `MIX_ENV=test mix test test/letflow/engine/snapshot_writer_test.exs` myself: real output was '10 tests, 0 failures' (Finished in 3.6 seconds), matching the 6 AC groups' test counts (1+2+2+1+2+2=10).
